Question ID: SPEECH_U06_L06_GP_Q01

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.DIG.01

A class needs to share quick instructions for joining an online speech rehearsal. Which digital format best fits the audience need?

answer.text: A. A long essay explaining the history of online meetings.

feedback.text: This format does not match the audience need. Students need quick instructions, not background information.

answer.text: B. A short digital checklist with the meeting link and steps.

feedback.text: Correct. A checklist fits the purpose because it gives students clear, usable steps for joining the rehearsal.

answer.text: C. A decorative poster with no link or instructions.

feedback.text: This may look interesting, but it fails the communication purpose. The audience needs practical joining information.

answer.text: D. A transcript of a full speech about technology.

feedback.text: This gives too much unrelated information. Audience-aware digital publication should select the format that helps users act.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U06_L06_GP_Q02

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.COM.03

Which choice best shows audience awareness for parents receiving an email about a presentation night?

answer.text: A. Use slang and inside jokes from class.

feedback.text: This tone may confuse or exclude parents. Audience awareness means choosing language that fits the readers and setting.

answer.text: B. Put the location at the very bottom after several unrelated details.

feedback.text: This hides important information. Parents need key event details placed where they can find them easily.

answer.text: C. Use vague wording such as "come to the thing later."

feedback.text: This does not communicate clearly. Audience-aware communication should make the event, time, and purpose specific.

answer.text: D. Use a clear subject line, respectful tone, date, location, and contact information.

feedback.text: Correct. This choice fits the audience because it gives parents the information they need in a professional, usable form.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U06_L06_GP_Q03

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.PRES.02

Why should a slide deck about interview preparation use brief headings and simple visuals?

answer.text: A. They help the audience follow key points while the speaker explains details aloud.

feedback.text: Correct. The visuals support the presentation by guiding attention without replacing the speaker's explanation.

answer.text: B. They make it possible for the speaker to avoid explaining anything.

feedback.text: This misunderstands presentation support. Visuals should work with the speaker, not replace communication.

answer.text: C. They guarantee that every audience member will agree with the message.

feedback.text: This overclaims. Good visuals improve clarity, but they cannot guarantee agreement.

answer.text: D. They allow the presenter to include every detail on one slide.

feedback.text: This creates overload. Strong digital presentation design organizes information so the audience can follow it.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U06_L06_GP_Q04

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.DIG.01

Which design choice best supports accessibility in a digital publication?

answer.text: A. Use tiny text so more information fits on the page.

feedback.text: Tiny text makes the message harder to read. Accessibility requires the audience to see and use the information clearly.

answer.text: B. Use low contrast colors because they look subtle.

feedback.text: Low contrast can make text difficult to read. A clear publication uses readable contrast for the audience.

answer.text: C. Use readable text size, clear headings, and strong contrast.

feedback.text: Correct. These choices help the audience read, scan, and understand the digital publication more easily.

answer.text: D. Remove headings so the page looks less structured.

feedback.text: Headings support scanning and organization. Removing them can make the message harder for the audience to use.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U06_L06_GP_Q05

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.COM.03

Which question should a communicator ask before selecting a digital format?

answer.text: A. Which format lets me add the most decoration?

feedback.text: Decoration is not the first concern. The format should be chosen because it helps the audience understand and use the message.

answer.text: B. Who is the audience, and what do they need to know first?

feedback.text: Correct. Audience and priority information should guide the digital format, organization, and design choices.

answer.text: C. How can I make the message longer?

feedback.text: Length does not guarantee clarity. Audience-aware communication uses enough information, organized for the user's needs.

answer.text: D. Which platform is newest or most popular?

feedback.text: Popularity alone is not enough. The best platform is the one that fits the audience, purpose, and communication context.
